title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data (abstract page)
note: Fetched. Abstract page, v1 submitted 18 Oct 2026, one author, text under CC BY 4.0, 13 pages. Headline: picking the latest run issued before a GB auction gate selects a run not yet published on over 99% of delivery days for six of ten weather-model configurations at one of two gates; apparent accuracy effect between -9% and +24%. Links no code or data.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data (full text v1)
note: Fetched, full text. Setup: timestamps of 128,656 forecast runs (wind, solar, demand forecasts for GB from ten weather-model configurations) in one commercial vendor archive (Energy Quantified), matched to the N2EX day-ahead gate (09:50 UK time) and EPEX IDA1 gate (17:30) for 1,734 delivery days, Jan 2022 to Sep 2026. No forecasting model is fitted; no prices or trading results.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data (full text v1)
note: Table 2: median delay from issue to publication 2.75 h (ICON-SR), 2.76 (ICON), 3.55 (GFS), 3.86 (GFS-ENS), 5.42 to 6.72 h for the ECMWF and AIFS configurations; finalisation up to 2.7 h later. Delays drift: the four ECMWF configurations got 0.6 to 1.4 h faster after late 2024; the ICON 06 UTC run slowed from 2.68 to 3.20 h. 3.0% of runs have no finalisation time.

title: research: primary sources for and against the claim
note: One research call, standard tier, LinkedIn excluded, 12 sources. Agrees with the fetched paper: the numbers are the author's own from a proprietary archive; it found no code, data, Zenodo record, pre-registration, replication or critique. Says exchange and ECMWF schedules support the mechanism, not the percentages. Sources 6 to 12 (a hobby forum, unrelated repositories and pages) were not used.

title: Product Specifications GB Market, Nord Pool AS (research source 4)
note: Research source 4, then fetched. Exchange rulebook, effective 10 Jul 2023: times are UK clock time; GB day-ahead auction gate closure 09:50, SEM-GB intraday auctions IDA1 17:30 and IDA2 08:00. Matches the gate times the paper uses and its point that gates follow local time. Context, not the candidate's own record.

title: IFS Medium-range Control forecast and Analysis Data, Set I (research source 5)
note: Research source 5, then fetched. ECMWF product page: four control runs a day, hourly steps to 90 h; the dissemination-time table for atmospheric fields came back garbled, only the post-processed products were readable (00 UTC based available 06:55, 12 UTC based 18:55). Supports an hours-long lag between run time and availability in general; the 05:45 figure the paper cites was not confirmed here.

title: search: author repository for the paper (site:github.com)
note: One search restricted to github.com for the author's name with point-in-time leakage, publication time and gate closure, LinkedIn excluded, 20 results. No repository by the author or citing the paper. Results were unrelated GB wind-forecast dashboards and price-forecast projects that apply publish-time cutoffs; none replicates or tests this paper.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data (full text v1)
note: Other results. A run one day older is 25-35% less accurate for wind, about 10% for solar, 1.5-3% for demand; demand accuracy instead follows a daily cycle of run quality (GFS MAE 751, 787, 851, 920 MW for the 06, 12, 18, 00 UTC runs), cause not established. A 5-minute action margin can cost a six-hour cycle (ICON, summer day-ahead). Outturns are revised up to 32 days later.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data (full text v1)
note: Limits the author states: one vendor, one market, two gates; magnitudes are specific to that setting. Timestamp meaning checked by polling three runs on one evening. The archive keeps only final values, so values visible at the gate are not recovered; reference outturns are themselves revised. Value comparison: three deterministic configurations, zero margin. No downstream model or trading effect.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data (full text v1)
note: Availability and design: the data are a commercial archive pulled through the vendor's Python client, Jun to Oct 2026; no repository, data deposit or pre-registration is named in the text. The naive selections were archived by an earlier version of the author's own pipeline, so the study started from the author's own leak. Proposes an eight-step timestamp audit protocol.
